statement: The system shall provide in `NaruServe-servlet`, package `com.snoworca.naruserve.servlet`, the public final class `ServletAdapter` implementing `HttpAdapter`, the public `@FunctionalInterface ServletConfigurer` with `RestApp configure(RestApp.Builder builder) throws Exception`, and the public `NaruServeInitializer` implementing `javax.servlet.ServletContainerInitializer`, registered in `META-INF/services/javax.servlet.ServletContainerInitializer`, which reads the context init-parameters `naruserve.configurer`, `naruserve.urlPattern` and `naruserve.shutdownTimeoutSeconds`; the module has no `jakarta.servlet` counterpart in v1.
rationale: Covers D-358, D-363 (container registration and class names), wave decisions Servlet adapter decisions (r1 W2-007), Who builds the app on the Servlet adapter (r4 W2-003) and Servlet SSE registration (r4 W2-005); answers Q-4. Measured (2026-10-20): `NaruServe-servlet/src/main` holds only `package-info.java`; `build.gradle` declares `javax.servlet:javax.servlet-api:3.1.0` and `javax.websocket:javax.websocket-api:1.1` `compileOnly` for the module; a built `RestApp` has no adapter setter and `RestApp.Builder` takes `httpAdapter`, `jsonCodec` and `logger` (`RestApp.java:226-270`). Decision (C-07): the names are `ServletAdapter`, `ServletConfigurer`, `NaruServeInitializer` and the package-private `NaruServeServlet`; the initializer is discovered through the Servlet 3.0 service file, so an application only sets the init-parameter; `naruserve.urlPattern` defaults to `/*` and accepts `/*`, `/` or `/prefix/*`; the servlet is named `naruserve` and registered with `asyncSupported=true` and no `MultipartConfig`. Decision (C-07): the container's destroy callback calls `app.shutdown(timeout, SECONDS)` because `RestApp` has only `shutdown(long, TimeUnit)`; the timeout is `naruserve.shutdownTimeoutSeconds`, an integer from 1 to 300 with default 10 (the value `docs/api/app.md` uses; a bound exists because no limit may default to unlimited, I-012). When `naruserve.configurer` is absent the initializer does nothing, because the jar may sit in `WEB-INF/lib` of an application that does not use NaruServe. Pitfall: `@HandlesTypes` is not used, so no classpath scan runs at container start. Pitfall: `jetty-servlet` alone does not run `ServletContainerInitializer`s; the tests use a Jetty `WebAppContext` with the annotation configuration so that the services file is discovered, and containers other than Jetty 9.4 are not exercised (recorded in `docs/api/servlet.md`). Rejected alternative: a `ServletContextListener` declared in `web.xml` or by `@WebListener`; it needs the application to list it and `@WebListener` needs annotation scanning, which a jar in `WEB-INF/lib` loses when `metadata-complete=true`.
acceptanceCriteria: Reflection finds `ServletAdapter` public, final, implementing `com.snoworca.naruserve.spi.HttpAdapter` with a public no-argument constructor; `ServletConfigurer` a public interface annotated `@FunctionalInterface` whose only abstract method is `RestApp configure(RestApp.Builder)` declared `throws Exception`; `NaruServeInitializer` a public class implementing `javax.servlet.ServletContainerInitializer`; and package `com.snoworca.naruserve.servlet` annotated `@NullMarked`. [D-358; D-363]

The built module jar holds `META-INF/services/javax.servlet.ServletContainerInitializer` whose only line is `com.snoworca.naruserve.servlet.NaruServeInitializer`, read from the jar as `DefaultAppFactoryTest` reads the bootstrap services file. [D-363]

On an embedded Jetty 9.4 `WebAppContext` started with its annotation configuration (the `jetty-webapp` and `jetty-annotations` test dependencies of CON-SVL-001), the initializer is discovered from the services file without any test code naming it; a web application with the init-parameter `naruserve.configurer` registers exactly one servlet named `naruserve` mapped to `/*`, with `isAsyncSupported() == true` and no multipart configuration, and a web application without the init-parameter registers nothing and every request is answered by the container (`404`). Residual gap: other Servlet 3.1 containers are not exercised and `docs/api/servlet.md` says so. [D-363; r4 W2-005]

The init-parameter `naruserve.urlPattern` accepts `/*`, `/` and `/api/*` (mapping the servlet accordingly) and any other value (`api/*`, `*.json`, an empty string) makes context startup fail with a `ServletException` whose message names the parameter and the value. [D-363]

The init-parameter `naruserve.shutdownTimeoutSeconds` is an integer from 1 to 300 with default 10 and is the timeout of the `app.shutdown(timeout, SECONDS)` call that the container's destroy callback makes; any other value (`0`, `301`, `ten`, an empty string) makes context startup fail with a `ServletException` whose message names the parameter and the value. [D-359; D-363; I-012]

The initializer instantiates the class named by `naruserve.configurer` through its public no-argument constructor and hands it a `RestApp.Builder` that already holds a `ServletAdapter`; a missing class, a class that does not implement `ServletConfigurer`, a class without a public no-argument constructor, a `configure` that throws and a `configure` that returns `null` each make context startup fail with a `ServletException` whose message names the class. [D-359; r4 W2-003]

The build adds the class-reference prefix `jakarta/servlet/` for `:NaruServe-servlet` to the `classRefPrefixes` closure of `build.gradle` as a separate `if (path == ':NaruServe-servlet')` branch, leaving the pinned `:NaruServe-api` prefix line of `BuildLayoutTest` unchanged, so the existing `checkClassReferences` task fails the build, naming `Class -> jakarta/servlet/...`, when a main class of `NaruServe-servlet` references it; a negative fixture proves the check fails, and `settings.gradle` includes no module for `jakarta.servlet`. [D-358; I-002]

statement: The system shall start the app on the Servlet adapter when the container initialises the web application — the initializer installs the `ServletAdapter`, finds the Gson codec by reflection, calls the configurer and then `app.listen(0)`, so `onStart` runs and the state becomes `RUNNING` exactly as on the embedded engine — and shall run `app.shutdown(timeout, SECONDS)` with the timeout of `naruserve.shutdownTimeoutSeconds` (default 10) when the container destroys the web application; `ServletAdapter.bind` stores the handler and opens no socket, and `boundPort()` and `ServerHandle.port()` are `0`.
acceptanceCriteria: On the embedded container, context startup builds the app through the configurer and calls `app.listen(0)` before the first request: `onStart` callbacks have run once, `app.state()` is `RUNNING` and a request is served. [D-359]

Context destruction runs `app.shutdown(10, SECONDS)` (or the `naruserve.shutdownTimeoutSeconds` value): `onStop` callbacks run, the state is `TERMINATED`, `ServletAdapter.stop` and `release` have been called, `shutdown` returns within that timeout plus the margin of `docs/api/lifecycle.md`, and a second destruction is harmless. [D-359]

`ServletAdapter.boundPort()` throws `IllegalStateException` before any `bind` (the SPI contract of `HttpAdapter.boundPort`, FR-ENGINE-001 AC-5) and returns `0` after `bind`; `bind("127.0.0.1", 8080, handler)` and `bind(settings, handler)` return without starting a thread or opening a socket and ignore host and port, which a test asserts for the adapter alone; `ServerHandle.port()` of the app is `0`. [D-359; D-107; r3 W2-001]
A user call of `app.listen(8080)` on an app built with a `ServletAdapter` binds nothing, runs `onStart` and reaches `RUNNING` through the same path as the initializer. [D-359; r2 W2-001]

When `com.snoworca.naruserve.gson.GsonJsonCodec` is on the web application's class path the initializer finds it by reflection and presets it as the codec; the configurer may replace it with `Builder.jsonCodec`; when neither exists startup fails with a `ServletException` whose message contains `com.snoworca.naruserve.gson.GsonJsonCodec` and `jsonCodec`. The module `runtimeClasspath` stays `NaruServe-api` only. [r5 W2-002; I-005]

The app logger is the `ConsoleLogger` that `RestApp.Builder` defaults to when the configurer does not call `Builder.logger`, and a logger that the configurer sets is the one the app keeps. [r4 W2-003; FR-ENGINE-009]
A failing `onStart` callback (an `AppStartException` from `listen`) makes context startup fail with a `ServletException` that carries it as cause, and no thread of the app remains. [D-359; I-015]

Deviation (recorded): the frozen D-416 thread total of 451 (452 with the keeper thread, PERF-APP-001 AC-2) bounds the embedded TinyHttpd app; on the Servlet adapter the threads are the container's plus at most `maxSseStreams` SSE threads (FR-SVL-005), and `docs/api/servlet.md` says so. [D-416]

A handler's `res.status(201).header("X-A", "1").send("ok")` reaches the client as status `201`, header `X-A: 1` and body `ok` with the `Content-Length` the core set; a `res.stream` response of unknown length arrives with an intact body and without a `Content-Length` and `Transfer-Encoding` conflict (chunked framing is asserted only for a body larger than the container's output buffer or after a flush, because a container may buffer a small body and frame it with a length); and no error page of the container appears for a `404` or `500` the core produced, because `sendError` is never called. [D-360]
A HEAD request to a GET route returns the `Content-Length` of the GET body and no body bytes, and a `204` and a `304` carry no body, on the embedded container. [D-360; FR-HTTP-017]

After `abort()` (called from another thread while a body write is in progress) the write fails with `IOException`, a later `commit` and `finish` throw `IOException`, and `abort()` called twice is harmless; a second `commit`, `sendFile` or `eventStream` on one exchange throws `IllegalStateException`. [r2 W2-006]

`res.file` and `res.download` on a file serve the whole file, a single `Range` (`206` with `Content-Range`) and a `416`, byte for byte equal to the in-memory adapter, with `sendFile` copying in chunks of at most 64 KiB and never reading the file into memory; the class references no `java.nio.file` type. [D-360; FR-STATIC-010]
Response header order on the wire is the container's, `docs/api/servlet.md` says so, and no test of the shared case suite depends on header order. [r2 W2-006]

rationale: Covers D-359 (shutdown on container destroy), D-107 (two-call stop), wave decisions Servlet stop (r3 W2-003) and Blocked writes of a Servlet SSE stream (r5 W2-001), and I-012, I-015. Measured: the core shutdown sequence runs the before-wait participants (the SSE and WebSocket closing participants, FR-SSE-005) and then `adapter.stop(left(deadline))` (`internal/DefaultRestApp.java:682` `a.stop`, `:705` `a.release`, FR-APP-011). Deviation (recorded under I-012): a drain thread stuck in a socket write to a client that stopped reading is bounded only by the container's own write timeout, which the adapter does not control; the "cut at timeout" promise of `docs/api/sse.md` therefore holds on the Servlet adapter up to that container bound, and the release documentation lists the deviation (OPS-REL-007). Decision: the adapter counts in-flight `service()` calls and open streams under one lock and waits on its condition; refusing by `503` happens before the core handler runs, using the `ErrorRenderer` of the settings. Pitfall: `stop` called from the container's destroy callback may run on a container thread, so it must not wait for container-owned work beyond the deadline. Rejected alternative: interrupting container request threads at the deadline; interrupting a thread the container owns is unsafe.

Covers D-359, D-363, wave decisions Servlet adapter semantics left open (r2 W2-006) and Servlet bind (r4 W2-006). Measured (2026-10-20): `allowedHosts` is enforced only by the TinyHttpd adapter (`NaruServe-tinyhttpd/.../TinyHttpdAdapter.java:118-120`) and nowhere in `NaruServe-api/src/main` outside `ServerOptions` itself; `bindAddress` and `port` are applied only by the TinyHttpd adapter's bind (`:100`), but the core still logs a LAN warning for a non-loopback `bindAddress` (`internal/DefaultRestApp.java:499`) and `ServerHandle.address()` reports the configured address, so on the Servlet adapter both describe the setting, not the container; `ServerSettings` carries `maxSseStreams` (default 128), `logger` and `errorRenderer` (`spi/ServerSettings.java:32-56`). Decision: the ignored list in `servlet.md` names exactly the `ServerOptions` settings `bindAddress`, `allowedHosts`, `maxHeaderSize`, `maxHeaderCount`, `maxRequestLineLength`, `headerTimeout`, `bodyReadTimeout`, `writeTimeout`, `minBodyRate`, `maxWorkers`, `maxConnections`, `maxUpgradedConnections` and `maxConnectionsPerAddress`, plus the port argument of `listen`; the applied list names the body limit, `jsonLimit`, `formLimit`, `app.multipart`, `maxSseStreams`, the SSE options and `trustProxy`. Pitfall: because `allowedHosts` is an adapter setting, a Host allowlist the application relies on is not enforced behind a container; `servlet.md` tells the reader to configure virtual hosts in the container. Rejected alternative: enforcing `allowedHosts` in the Servlet adapter; the container owns the connector and virtual host, and a second enforcement would diverge from it.
statement: The system shall override `HttpAdapter.bind(ServerSettings, ExchangeHandler)` on the Servlet adapter to keep the frozen settings it uses — `maxSseStreams` and the `ErrorRenderer` (and logger) — while `bind(host, port, handler)` only stores the handler, and shall ignore every `ServerOptions` setting that configures the embedded engine (`bindAddress`, `allowedHosts`, `maxHeaderSize`, `maxHeaderCount`, `maxRequestLineLength`, `headerTimeout`, `bodyReadTimeout`, `writeTimeout`, `minBodyRate`, `maxWorkers`, `maxConnections`, `maxUpgradedConnections` and `maxConnectionsPerAddress`), listed as ignored in `docs/api/servlet.md`, while the body limit, the JSON limit and the multipart limits still apply in the core.
acceptanceCriteria: Reflection finds that `ServletAdapter` declares its own `bind(ServerSettings, ExchangeHandler)`, and a test shows that the adapter used `maxSseStreams(3)` (a fourth stream is refused, FR-SVL-005) and the settings' `ErrorRenderer` (a custom renderer's body appears in the adapter's own `503` and `404` answers). [r4 W2-006; D-363]

A test sets `allowedHosts("example.test")`, `bindAddress("10.255.255.1")`, `maxWorkers(1)` and `maxHeaderSize(1024)` on the app and shows the Servlet adapter serves a request with another `Host` header and a normal header block unchanged, so these settings have no effect there. [r2 W2-006]
The body limit still applies: a body above `app.bodyLimit` answers `413`, the JSON limit answers `413` and the multipart limits apply, on the embedded container. [D-363; r1 W2-007]

`docs/api/servlet.md` lists the 13 ignored `ServerOptions` settings by exactly the names above and the applied settings (`app.bodyLimit`, `jsonLimit`, `formLimit`, `app.multipart`, `maxSseStreams`, the SSE options, `trustProxy`), and a docs test checks that every listed name exists on `ServerOptions` or `RestApp`, so the list cannot drift. [D-363]

`docs/api/servlet.md` states that the core's LAN warning for a non-loopback `bindAddress` and `ServerHandle.address()` describe the configured setting, not the container's connector, and a test shows that a default app logs no such warning on the Servlet adapter. [r2 W2-006]

rationale: Covers D-375, wave decision Release plugins (r4 W2-004), I-019 and T50. Measured (2026-10-20): the nine published modules are the entries of `naruModules` in `build.gradle:11-12`; the Gradle plugin portal metadata lists `org.cyclonedx:cyclonedx-gradle-plugin` up to 3.5.1 and the network was reachable; `build.gradle` has a `plugins {}` block with `ru.vyarus.animalsniffer` and the Kotlin plugin `apply false`. Decision: the plugin is applied from `gradle/release.gradle`, a script plugin with its own `buildscript {}` block, because a `plugins {}` block cannot be conditional and resolves its plugin even with `apply false`; `gradle/release.gradle` is not a module build file, so CON-BUILD-017 AC-2 (no `build.gradle` in a module directory) holds; CON-BUILD-003 AC-1 (the root `build.gradle` holds every module's configuration) would read false once release tasks live in the applied script, so wave 8 supersedes CON-BUILD-003 with CON-BUILD-017, whose AC-1 states the one exception, and the line of `CLAUDE.md` that says the root `build.gradle` configures all modules gets the same exception sentence. The plugin version is an exact literal pinned when the file is written (not a dynamic range); the SBOM files go to `build/reports/naruserve/sbom/<module>.cdx.json`; the lifecycle task names are `releaseSbom`, `releaseScan`, `releaseLicenses` and `releaseCheck`. Pitfall: `BuildLayoutTest` reads `build.gradle` for pinned strings (`'java-library'`, `options.release = 8`, the class-reference prefixes), so the conditional apply is added without touching them. Rejected alternative: a `buildscript { classpath }` in the root file; it resolves the plugin on every build, including offline.
acceptanceCriteria: `./gradlew -Prelease releaseSbom` writes one CycloneDX JSON file per published module — nine files named `<module>.cdx.json` under `build/reports/naruserve/sbom/`, one for each entry of `naruModules` — each with `bomFormat` `CycloneDX` and a component for every `runtimeClasspath` dependency of that module (Gson 2.14.0 for `NaruServe-gson`, `kotlin-stdlib` for `NaruServe-kotlin`, `slf4j-api` for `NaruServe-slf4j`, the TinyHttpd components for `NaruServe-tinyhttpd`), and none for `compileOnly` or test-scope artifacts (the Servlet API and Jetty). [D-375; T50]
The run is recorded with its command, date, file list and component counts in `docs/release/test-results.md` under T50, because the plugin cannot be resolved by the default build. [D-375; D-381]

A default-build test asserts that `build.gradle` contains the conditional `apply from: 'gradle/release.gradle'` guarded by `project.hasProperty('release')`, that the strings `cyclonedx` and `dependencycheck` occur in no file of the root build except `gradle/release.gradle`, that `gradle/release.gradle` pins each plugin version as an exact literal, and that no release task is a dependency of `check`, `build` or `test`. [r4 W2-004; I-019]
`./gradlew build --offline` with a Gradle user home that holds neither plugin succeeds, which a recorded run (command, date, exit code) shows for the release machine. [r4 W2-004; I-019]

The default `./gradlew build` still passes `BuildLayoutTest` unchanged, including `con_BUILD_003_AC1_rootBuildFileHoldsPluginsCompileDependenciesAndChecks` and `con_BUILD_003_AC2_noModuleBuildFile` (re-pointed to CON-BUILD-017), and a new check in it asserts the conditional apply of AC-3. [CON-BUILD-017]

rationale: Covers D-376, wave decision Release scan and result rows (r3 W2-005: pending for any reason the scanner cannot finish) and T50; the block on findings is FR-REL-003. Measured (2026-10-20): the Gradle plugin portal lists `org.owasp:dependency-check-gradle` up to 13.0.0; the network was reachable but a scan without an NVD API key is rate-limited and can fail partway; the shipped runtime dependencies are Gson 2.14.0 with `com.google.errorprone:error_prone_annotations:2.48.0`, `kotlin-stdlib` 2.2.0 with `org.jetbrains:annotations:13.0`, `slf4j-api` 1.7.36 and the TinyHttpd components, as `build/reports/naruserve/dependency-graphs.txt` lists them per module and configuration. Decision: the pure parts — the report writer, the pending decision and the dependency-list derivation — are plain Java 8 sources in `gradle/release-tools` (package `com.snoworca.naruserve.release`), which the root `test` source set adds as a source directory and which `gradle/release.gradle` compiles and calls, so the default build can test them without any plugin or network. Decision: the committed record of the release run is `docs/release/vulnerability-scan.md`, copied from the build report; the scan covers the `runtimeClasspath` of the nine published modules and excludes test scope (Jetty 9.4 of the Servlet tests); the scanner's own failure is caught by a wrapper task that writes the pending report. Pitfall: Dependency-Check fails the build on an update error by default; the wrapper converts that into `pending`, otherwise an offline release machine could not record anything. Rejected alternative: treating a pending scan as a pass; the record says `pending`, T50 stays `manual-pending` for this part and I-020 forbids promoting a requirement on a pending check.
acceptanceCriteria: With the scanner stubbed to fail for each of four causes — no network, a missing NVD API key, a rate limit and a tool error — the report writer in `gradle/release-tools` produces a report whose status line is `pending`, whose reason line names the cause, and whose dependency list equals the sorted union of the `group:name:version` of the `runtimeClasspath` entries of the nine published modules in `dependency-graphs.txt`, which a default-build test over the writer asserts without network. [D-376; r3 W2-005]

A finished scan produces the status `completed` with a findings table (dependency, identifier, CVSS score, severity), or the sentence `no findings`, and the report names the scanner version and the data timestamp. [D-376]

`docs/release/vulnerability-scan.md` exists and holds the report of the release run (`pending` with the reason, or `completed`), and the T50 vulnerability line of `docs/release/test-results.md` is `manual-pending` when the report is `pending` and `automated` or `verified` when it is `completed`, which a docs test compares. [D-376; D-381]
The report's dependency list excludes `compileOnly` and test-scope artifacts (the Servlet API, JSpecify, JUnit, Jetty) and includes the TinyHttpd components. [D-376]

statement: The release build shall fail `./gradlew -Prelease releaseCheck` while the vulnerability report shows a High or Critical finding (CVSS 7.0 or higher) for a runtime dependency of a published module that has no recorded exception in `docs/release/vulnerability-exceptions.md`, where an exception names the vulnerability id, the dependency, the reason, the approver and the date; a `pending` scan does not block the build but is shown as pending, never as passed.

[D-377]

A fixture report with the status `pending` makes the check pass and prints `scan pending: release not cleared for T50 vulnerability part`, and the release notes list the scan as pending. [D-377; r3 W2-005]

The check reads only the runtime dependencies of the published modules, so a High finding in a test-scope artifact does not block, which a fixture asserts. [D-377]

statement: The release build shall run `./gradlew -Prelease releaseLicenses`, which resolves the license of every dependency on the `runtimeClasspath` of the published modules, fails when any has a GPL-family license (GPL, LGPL or AGPL) or none that can be determined, and writes `THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md` at the repository root listing each shipped dependency as `group:name:version` with its license name and URL, and a default-build test shall fail when that file does not list exactly those dependencies.
rationale: Covers D-378 and T50. Measured (2026-10-20): the root `LICENSE` and `/Users/beom/work/git/TinyHttpd/LICENSE` both open "BSD 3-Clause License"; Gson, `com.google.errorprone:error_prone_annotations:2.48.0` (Gson's transitive dependency), `kotlin-stdlib` and `org.jetbrains:annotations:13.0` are Apache-2.0 and `slf4j-api` 1.7.36 is MIT by their POMs; `javax.servlet-api` 3.1.0 (CDDL with GPLv2 classpath exception) is `compileOnly` and therefore provided by the container, not shipped; `build.gradle` already writes the resolved graphs to `build/reports/naruserve/dependency-graphs.txt` (`checkDependencyRules`). Decision: licenses come from the POMs through an artifact resolution query; the TinyHttpd components come from an override table in `gradle/release.gradle` with the source `TinyHttpd/LICENSE` (the included build has no POM); a component with no license information and no override fails the task; the file also lists the compile-only artifacts under "provided by the container or the build, not shipped" with their licenses so the CDDL/GPL entry is explicit. Pitfall: a dependency whose POM states two licenses (dual license) passes when at least one is non-GPL and the file lists both. Rejected alternative: a name-based allowlist of group ids; a new transitive dependency would pass unseen.
acceptanceCriteria: `releaseLicenses` writes `THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md` with one row per shipped dependency taken from the `runtimeClasspath` entries of `dependency-graphs.txt` — Gson 2.14.0, `error_prone_annotations` 2.48.0, `kotlin-stdlib` 2.2.0, `org.jetbrains:annotations` 13.0, `slf4j-api` 1.7.36 and the TinyHttpd components — giving license name and URL, and a section of provided artifacts that names `javax.servlet-api` as container-provided and not shipped. [D-378; T50]

The license check, exercised by a default-build test over its decision function in `gradle/release-tools` with fixtures, fails for GPL-2.0, LGPL-3.0 and AGPL-3.0 and for an unknown license, and passes for Apache-2.0, MIT, BSD-3-Clause and a dual license with one non-GPL member. [D-378]

A default-build test compares the dependency list parsed from `build/reports/naruserve/dependency-graphs.txt` (the shipped runtime dependencies) with the rows of `THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md` and fails, naming the dependency, on a missing or extra row, so the committed file cannot go stale. [D-378; I-005]
The run of `releaseLicenses` on the release machine is recorded under T50 in `docs/release/test-results.md` with its command and result. [D-378; D-381]

rationale: Covers D-382 and the Platform matrix of object.md §17.1, and wave decisions Release documentation statement (r1 W1-005). Measured (2026-10-20): the build machine has one JDK, OpenJDK 17.0.20 (`java -version`; `/usr/libexec/java_home -V` finds no other), so no Java 8 runtime ran the suite; the bytecode target is Java 8 by `options.release = 8` (CON-BUILD-004). Decision: the Java 8 row status is `pending` until a Java 8 run is recorded, then `verified` with that record as evidence; meanwhile the row cites the two compile-time checks and the command that produced them. The matrix uses the four literals of OPS-REL-003 (`automated`, `manual-pending`, `verified`, `out-of-v1-scope`) plus `pending` for a row whose run has not happened. Pitfall: `--release 8` proves the API surface and bytecode level, not runtime behaviour on a Java 8 JVM (for example Java 8 canonical path caching, FR-STATIC-006); the row must say so. Rejected alternative: marking the row `verified` because the bytecode is Java 8; D-382 forbids it.
acceptanceCriteria: `docs/release/release-notes.md` has a platform-matrix table with the five rows of §17.1 and a status column that uses only `automated`, `verified`, `pending`, `manual-pending` or `out-of-v1-scope`; the Java 8 row reads `pending` with the sentence that no Java 8 runtime ran, naming `--release 8` and `android-api-level-21` animal-sniffer as compile-time evidence and the JDK that did run (17). [D-382]

rationale: Restates CON-BUILD-003 AC-2 unchanged and changes AC-1 (D-003, D-004; wave decision Release plugins r4 W2-004, FR-REL-001). Frozen: the root build.gradle configures every module. Deviation (recorded): the release-only tasks (CycloneDX SBOM, vulnerability scan, license report) live in gradle/release.gradle, applied from the root build.gradle only when -Prelease is set, because a plugins block cannot be conditional and resolves its plugin even with apply false, which would make a default offline ./gradlew build resolve the release plugins (I-019). gradle/release.gradle is a script plugin, not a module build file, so AC-2 holds. Measured (2026-10-20): BuildLayoutTest con_BUILD_003_AC1 asserts only that the root build.gradle contains 'java-library', 'org.jetbrains.kotlin.jvm', 'ru.vyarus.animalsniffer', 'options.release = 8', 'checkClassReferences', 'checkDependencyRules' and 'configureDependencies', and con_BUILD_003_AC2 that no module directory holds a build file; both keep passing and are re-pointed to this requirement, plus a new check for the conditional apply. CLAUDE.md line on the root build file gets the same exception sentence. Rejected alternative: a buildscript classpath or an apply-false plugins entry in the root file; it resolves the plugin on every build.
